findings.anchor: .loop/plans/antigravity-okf-stop-hook.md (Intent, "continues only on the first stop of a turn")
findings.claim: The guard rests on executionNum 0 meaning "the first stop of a turn", but the spikes only show it for one turn. Both spikes ran `agy -p`, a single user turn; spike 2 shows a forced continue moves executionNum from 0 to 1, so the counter counts executor runs, and nothing shows it goes back to 0 when the user sends the next message. If it keeps counting through a conversation, the hook fires only on the first turn of an interactive session and is idle on every turn after that. Then the plan's contract ("continues only on the first stop of a turn") is false and the guard needs another design, such as state keyed by conversationId. The plan does not list this risk. It can be settled by running code: spike a two-turn conversation (a second message to the same conversation, by resume or an interactive run) with the logging Stop handler from spike 2, and record executionNum on the first stop of turn 2.

Nothing showed executionNum goes back to 0 on a later turn of the same conversation. Spike 3 settles it: in one conversation (agy -p, then agy -c -p, same conversationId on all four Stop calls) the stops carried executionNum 0, 1 in turn 1 and 0, 1 in turn 2, and the hook continued once per turn. The guard on executionNum 0 means the first stop of each turn.

The new detail string went into the Claude check, not the Antigravity one. claude.hook now says it holds "the SessionStart hook and okf's Stop check this kmctl writes", which is false because kmctl writes no Stop hook for Claude Code. antigravity.hook (doctor.py:486) still says it holds only "the SessionStart hook". The sample doctor output in the install how-to (lines 359 and 366) no longer matches either.

drop_apm_okf_stop sets `changed` once for the whole file and then tests `if changed and not events`. Once any okf handler is removed, every later named hook that was already empty gets deleted too. Running it on {"apm":{"Stop":[okf]},"keep":{}} leaves no "keep" key, which breaks r2's "keeps every other hook and key". Track the change per named hook instead, and add a test case for a hook that was empty to begin with.

Row r1's command (`-k okf_stop`) does not run test_plugin_folder_hooks_hold_one_flat_sessionstart_handler, the only test that checks the plugin folder's hooks.json has exactly the two named hooks with flat handlers. So r1's "a hook is missing or extra, the handler is not flat" goes unchecked by r1. The full test gate does cover it, and that test's name now describes only one of the two hooks. Rename it, or add an okf_stop test for the structure.

apm_okf_stop_present matches the raw text of .agents/hooks.json, but drop_apm_okf_stop skips a file that is not valid JSON. So when that file is unparsable but mentions okf-stop-check.sh, antigravity.apm-hooks fails and names `kmctl plugin install` as the fix, and install leaves the file alone. Either have doctor parse the file the same way install does, or have the fix name the file to repair by hand.
